_comment: Jellyfin reads logging.json in preference to logging.default.json, and
unlike that file this one is not replaced on upgrade. It is a full copy
of the shipped defaults with ONE change, marked below.
Why: Jellyfin writes two Serilog sinks with different templates. The
file sink carries a full date; the console sink carried only HH:mm:ss.
CrowdSec reads the console sink via the Docker datasource, and
LePresidente/jellyfin-logs expects the file sink's format -- its
JELLYFIN_CUSTOMDATE grok is YEAR-MONTHNUM-MONTHDAY HOUR:MINUTE:SECOND.
The date group is optional so the message still matched, but
evt.StrTime came back empty and dateparse-enrich failed. Live
detection was unaffected (CrowdSec falls back to arrival time);
forensic replay of an old log collapsed every event to the replay time.
Copied into the jellyfin_config volume by set_logging.sh -- this file
is the source of truth, the volume holds a copy. See the crowdsec
stack README for the full diagnosis.
THE ONE CHANGE: the Console sink's outputTemplate timestamp was
{Timestamp:HH:mm:ss} and is now {Timestamp:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff zzz},
identical to the File sink. Everything else is verbatim defaults.
Comments live at this top level on purpose. Serilog binds the keys
inside a sink's Args to that sink method's PARAMETERS, so a stray
_comment in there can fail the sink outright and take console
logging with it. Only the Serilog section is read; this key is not.
